original_text: The content of any electronic and/or print versions of the present document shall not be modified without the prior written authorization of ETSI.

attribute_scores.rationale: The restriction against unauthorized modification is clear, though it addresses administrative policy rather than software behavior.
Lacks operational context on how a software system would enforce or verify compliance with document modification restrictions.
Terminologically aligned with standard document copyright and control statements.
Uses the normative modal verb 'shall', but lacks standard syntactic condition-subject-action structure for system requirements.
Factually and legally accurate regarding ETSI document distribution policies.
Combines electronic and print media into a single requirement statement using conjunctions and disjunctions.
Verifiable through legal/administrative inspection, but generally unfeasible or out of scope for automated software verification.

shortcomings.explanation: The requirement conflates two distinct media types (electronic versions and print versions) into a single statement, violating the singularity principle by combining multiple applicability domains.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: The content of any electronic and/or print versions of the present document shall not be modified
shortcomings.explanation: The statement acts as a legal disclaimer or document governance rule rather than a software requirement. It fails to specify system inputs, triggers, or automated enforcement mechanisms required for functional SRS inclusion.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: The requirement governs the administrative/legal constraints regarding the immutability and distribution of ETSI MEC specifications documentation. Within a technical software requirements specification (SRS) for a multi-access edge computing system, this functions as a standard legal/copyright compliance notice rather than a technical system capability.

evaluations.context_reasoning: The flagged phrasing 'electronic and/or print versions' groups related dissemination formats into a single administrative restriction. Separating this into two requirements would be pedantic and offer zero practical benefit to the implementation, testing, or compliance of the document governance policy.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: The content of any electronic and/or print versions of the present document shall not be modified
evaluations.context_reasoning: While this statement functions as a legal/copyright governance rule rather than a software functionality with automated triggers, it is a mandatory administrative requirement in standards-developing organizations (ETSI). Applying strict software-only SRS rules to document front-matter governance clauses is a false positive based on document context.

discarded_defects.explanation: The requirement conflates two distinct media types (electronic versions and print versions) into a single statement, violating the singularity principle by combining multiple applicability domains.

discarded_defects.explanation: The statement acts as a legal disclaimer or document governance rule rather than a software requirement. It fails to specify system inputs, triggers, or automated enforcement mechanisms required for functional SRS inclusion.

layer2.reasoning_summary: Both candidate defects are discarded. DEF-1 is overly pedantic regarding the grouping of document formats ('electronic and/or print'), which is standard legal boilerplate for document governance and does not impede clarity. DEF-2 flags the requirement as a legal disclaimer rather than an automated software function; however, in ETSI specifications, front-matter regulatory and copyright notices are standard structural requirements mandated by publishing standards rather than functional software specs, rendering automated enforcement inapplicable.
